'''Chiara Rosanna Nappi''' (born 21 February 1951) is an Italian [[physicist]].  Her research areas have included [[mathematical physics]], [[particle physics]], and [[string theory]].

==Academic career==
Nappi obtained the Diploma della Scuola di Perfezionamento in physics from the [[University of Naples Federico II|University of Naples]] in 1976. Her advisor was [[Giovanni Jona-Lasinio]] of the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]]. She moved to the [[United States]] to carry out academic research, first at [[Harvard University]], and later at [[Princeton University]] and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. She has since been a professor of physics at the [[University of Southern California]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://physics.usc.edu/Faculty/Nappi/|title=Chiara Nappi - Professor|date=2002-07-24|publisher=USC Physics|access-date=2009-01-14}}</ref> (1999–2001) and [[Princeton University]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.princeton.edu/physics/people/faculty/chiara-nappi/|title=Physics Department, Princeton University - Chiara Nappi|date=2009-11-23|publisher=Princeton Physics|access-date=2010-05-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100528043249/http://www.princeton.edu/physics/people/faculty/chiara-nappi/|archive-date=2010-05-28|url-status=dead}}</ref> (2001–present). In May 2013, Nappi obtained emerita status in Princeton.<ref>[https://dof.princeton.edu/sites/dof/files/Chiara%20Rosanna%20Nappi%202013%20Book.pdf Princeton University Honors Faculty Members Receiving Emeritus Status, May 2013]</ref>

==Research==
Chiara Nappi's early work focused on rigorous [[statistical mechanics]]. Her work with R. Figari and R. Hoegh-Krohn resulted in one of the first proposals of a thermal interpretation of [[quantum field theory]] in [[de Sitter space]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Figari|first=R. |author2=R. Hoegh-Krohn |author3=C. R. Nappi|date=1975-02-11|title=Interacting Relativistic Boson Fields In The De Sitter Universe With Two Space-Time Dimensions|journal=[[Communications in Mathematical Physics]]|doi=10.1007/BF01609830|url=http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS/Repository/1.0/Disseminate?handle=euclid.cmp/1103899347&view=body&content-type=pdf_1|volume=44|issue=3 |pages=265–278|bibcode = 1975CMaPh..44..265F |hdl=10852/44044 |s2cid=122179335 |hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In the 1980s, with G. Adkins and [[Edward Witten|E. Witten]], she investigated the static properties of [[baryons]] in the [[Skyrmion|Skyrme model]],<ref>{{cite journal|last=Adkins|first=G. |author2=C. R. Nappi |author3=E. Witten|date=1983-12-05|title=Static Properties of Nucleons in the Skyrme Model|journal=[[Nuclear Physics B]]|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(83)90559-X|volume=228|issue=3 |pages=552–566|bibcode = 1983NuPhB.228..552A }}</ref> and with A. Abouelsaood, C. G. Callan, and S. A. Yost, she worked on the behavior of [[String (physics)|open strings]] in background [[electromagnetic fields]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Abouelsaood|first=A.|author2=C. G. Callan |author3=C. R. Nappi |author4=S. A. Yost |date=1986-11-06|title=Open Strings in Background Gauge Fields|journal=[[Nuclear Physics B]]|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(87)90164-7|volume=280|pages=599–624|bibcode = 1987NuPhB.280..599A }}</ref>  She has also contributed to the analysis of [[Black hole|black hole solutions]] and [[noncommutative quantum field theory|noncommutativity]] in [[string theory]] and integrability in string theories and [[Gauge theory|gauge theories]].<ref>http://inspirehep.net/search?p=find+a+nappi,+chiara INSPIRE-HEP Database</ref> Nappi has also written a number of articles on education<ref>{{cite book|last=Nappi|first=Chiara|title=Why Charter Schools? The Princeton Story|year=1999|publisher=The Thomas B. Fordham Institute|url=http://www.edexcellencemedia.net/publications/1999/199910_whycharterschools/wcs.pdf|access-date=2013-02-25}}</ref> and women in science.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Nappi|first=Chiara|date=May 1990|title=On Mathematics and Science Education in the US and Europe|journal=[[Physics Today]]|doi=10.1063/1.2810564|volume=43|issue=5|page=77|bibcode = 1990PhT....43e..77N }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Nappi is married to [[Edward Witten]], a mathematical physicist and professor at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]].  They have three children, [[Ilana B. Witten|Ilana]], [[Daniela Witten|Daniela]], and Rafael.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.notablebiographies.com/newsmakers2/2006-Ra-Z/Witten-Edward.html|title=Edward Witten Biography|publisher=Advameg, Inc.|access-date=2010-05-13}}</ref>
